BOX 18.7  CLINICAL APPLICATIONS
Sodium and Phosphate Additives in Foods
Phosphate additives in foods have
become a mainstay in the U.S. food
supply. In 1990, phosphate additives 
contributed an estimated 470 mg of
phosphorus/day to the diet. Increased
use of these phosphate additives could
now contribute up to 1,000 mg/day of
phosphorus depending upon one’s food
choices. This is a concern for the gen-
eral population, but especially for CKD
patients. Restructured meats (chicken
nuggets and hotdogs), processed and
spreadable cheeses, “instant” products
(puddings and sauces), refrigerated
bakery products, and beverages are
products commonly enhanced with
phosphorus additives.
